svg.title: Deep Learning for Time Series 2026 — A Map of Methods
svg.desc: A map of recent deep learning for time series in six branches: lightweight baselines, patch transformers, state space models, foundation models, generative forecasting and multimodal approaches.
svg.text: Deep Learning for Time Series 2026 — A Map of Methods
What changed — patching · the return of state space · pretrained zero-shot · Diffusion generation
A · Lightweight baselines are still strong
A single linear layer matches transformers on long-horizon forecasting
A tabular forecaster pretrained on synthetic data
At high frequencies, statistical baselines still lead
Segments bundled into patches as tokens · channel independent
Attention over the variate axis, not time
The patch implicitly fixes which frequencies the model fits
C · The return of recurrence and state space
Selective state space — linear in length
Constant cost per patch, streaming updates
Competes with large models at around 9M parameters
Regime sensitive — without adjustment, performance is erratic
Multivariate and covariate support, single-pass quantiles
200M decoder · 16k context / small but strong encoder
Draw samples to build a distribution over paths
A new axis of generative forecasting, e.g. Sundial
Intervals in a single forward pass
Buy accuracy with more samples and ensembling
News and descriptions as conditioning in the same model
Attempts to automate model choice and preprocessing
GIFT-Eval compares zero-shot forecasting on common ground across 55 datasets and 97 tasks.
Recent reports put Chronos-2 ahead of TimesFM-2.5 and TiRex, and small Moirai-2 near larger models.
Complementary benchmarks built on realistic tasks, such as fev-bench, are used alongside it.
① Leakage — if the pretraining corpus overlaps the benchmark test window, zero-shot scores are inflated.
② Frequency — at second- and minute-level frequencies, statistical baselines still often win.
③ Finance — returns have an extremely low signal-to-noise ratio, so general benchmark scores do not transfer.
Supplementary track · public sources as of September 2026 — only representative model families are named.
Practical default: build statistical and lightweight baselines first, attach a foundation model zero-shot, and fine-tune only once the gain is confirmed.
